paragraphs.paragraph: The psalm opens with thanksgiving and the declaration of God’s wondrous works, then presents God’s promise to judge uprightly and His sustaining power over the earth’s pillars.
paragraphs.title: Thanksgiving and the Promise of Divine Judgment

easy.explanation: They give thanks because God’s name is near.
easy.q: What do the speakers give thanks for?

easy.explanation: He says, “When I shall receive the congregation I will judge uprightly.”
easy.q: What does the psalmist say he will do when he receives the congregation?

easy.explanation: He says, “I bear up the pillars of it.”
easy.q: What does the psalmist say he bears up?

answers: Raising the horns of the wicked
medium.explanation: The verse connects thanksgiving with declaring God’s wondrous works.
medium.q: What is connected with giving thanks in the opening verse?

medium.explanation: “Uprightly” describes judgment that is right and fair.
medium.q: What does “uprightly” mean in “I will judge uprightly”?

answers: God sustains the order of the earth
medium.explanation: The psalmist says he bears up the pillars of the earth, showing sustaining power.
medium.q: What does the statement about the earth’s pillars show?

answers: Thanksgiving, judgment, and divine sustaining power
challenge.explanation: The passage moves from thanksgiving to judgment and then to God’s support of the earth.
challenge.q: What progression appears in these verses?

challenge.explanation: The word “uprightly” indicates righteous and fair judgment.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the promise to judge uprightly?

answers: Both display God’s authority and order
The pillars prove judgment is impossible
challenge.explanation: The passage presents God as both righteous Judge and sustainer of the earth.
challenge.q: How are judgment and the pillars of the earth related?

paragraphs.idea: The psalm opens with thanksgiving and the declaration of God’s wondrous works, then presents God’s promise to judge uprightly and His sustaining power over the earth’s pillars.

paragraphs.paragraph: The psalmist warns fools and the wicked not to act foolishly, lift up their horns, or speak with a stiff neck in arrogant boasting.
paragraphs.title: A Warning Against Pride and Boasting

easy.explanation: The verse says, “I said unto the fools,” and then addresses the wicked.
easy.q: To whom is the warning addressed?

easy.explanation: They are told, “Lift not up the horn.”
easy.q: What are the wicked told not to lift up?

easy.explanation: The next verse says, “speak not with a stiff neck.”
easy.q: How are they told not to speak?

medium.explanation: Both images describe self-exaltation and arrogant speech.
medium.q: What do lifting up the horn and speaking with a stiff neck have in common?

medium.explanation: The expression suggests stubbornness, defiance, and pride.
medium.q: What does “a stiff neck” suggest in this context?

medium.explanation: The warning concerns lifting oneself up and speaking arrogantly.
medium.q: What kind of behavior is condemned in these verses?

answers: Pride appears in conduct as well as words
challenge.explanation: Lifting the horn represents proud conduct, while a stiff neck represents arrogant speech.
challenge.q: Why does the warning address both actions and speech?

answers: Power should not be used for arrogant self-exaltation
Power should always be displayed publicly
Personal power is the source of judgment
challenge.explanation: The wicked are warned not to exalt themselves or boast.
challenge.q: What view of personal power is taught here?

answers: They are called to stop their proud behavior
They are praised for their wisdom
challenge.explanation: Both groups are addressed as people who must abandon arrogant conduct.
challenge.q: What do the fools and the wicked share in this warning?

paragraphs.idea: The psalmist warns fools and the wicked not to act foolishly, lift up their horns, or speak with a stiff neck in arrogant boasting.

paragraphs.paragraph: Promotion does not come from the directions of the world or from outward sources of power, because God alone is the Judge who brings one person down and raises another up.
paragraphs.title: God Is the Source of Humbling and Exaltation

easy.explanation: The verse plainly says, “God is the judge.”
easy.q: Who is the Judge according to these verses?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “he putteth down one.”
easy.q: What does God do to one person?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “and setteth up another.”
easy.q: What does God do to another person?

medium.explanation: The directions are mentioned to show that promotion does not come from worldly directions.
medium.q: What do the east, west, and south represent in the passage?

answers: Being raised to a higher position
medium.explanation: Here, promotion means being exalted or raised up.
medium.q: What does “promotion” mean in this context?

medium.explanation: God is the Judge who determines each person’s position.
medium.q: What is the reason one person is put down and another is raised up?

answers: God determines human exaltation and downfall
The directions of the earth control destiny
challenge.explanation: The passage rejects outward sources and identifies God as the one who raises and lowers.
challenge.q: What view of authority is emphasized in these verses?

answers: It shows that judgment is not controlled by external powers
It proves that judgment does not exist
It makes the south the supreme judge
challenge.explanation: The directions cannot grant promotion; God alone judges.
challenge.q: How does the rejection of the directions support the theme of judgment?

challenge.explanation: The verse contrasts God putting one down with setting another up.
challenge.q: What is the central contrast in the final statement?

paragraphs.idea: Promotion does not come from the directions of the world or from outward sources of power, because God alone is the Judge who brings one person down and raises another up.

paragraphs.paragraph: The Lord’s cup contains mixed wine and represents judgment. The wicked drink its dregs, while the psalmist promises to declare God’s works and sing praises; the wicked’s horns will be cut off, but the righteous will be exalted.
paragraphs.title: The Cup of Judgment and the Song of Praise

easy.explanation: The verse says, “in the hand of the LORD there is a cup.”
easy.q: What is in the hand of the Lord?

answers: All the wicked of the earth
easy.explanation: The verse says the wicked of the earth shall drink them.
easy.q: Who will drink the dregs of the cup?

answers: Declare and sing praises to God
easy.explanation: He says, “I will declare for ever; I will sing praises to the God of Jacob.”
easy.q: What does the psalmist promise to do forever?

medium.explanation: The cup is an image of the Lord’s poured-out judgment.
medium.q: What does the cup represent in the passage?

answers: The sediment or last residue at the bottom
The servants who guard the cup
medium.explanation: Dregs are the residue left at the bottom of a cup.
medium.q: What are the “dregs” of the cup?

answers: The wicked are cut down and the righteous are exalted
The wicked are exalted and the righteous disappear
Both receive exactly the same outcome
medium.explanation: The wicked’s horns are cut off, while the horns of the righteous are exalted.
medium.q: What contrast appears between the wicked and the righteous at the end?

answers: The wicked receive judgment while the psalmist praises God and the righteous are exalted
The righteous are silent while the wicked sing praise
The cup is empty while the earth is full
challenge.explanation: The section joins judgment on the wicked with praise and exaltation for the righteous.
challenge.q: What major contrast structures this section?

answers: He distinguishes his faithful response from the fate of the wicked
He joins the wicked in drinking the cup
challenge.explanation: The phrase introduces the psalmist’s resolve to declare and sing praises to God.
challenge.q: What does “But I will” reveal about the psalmist’s response?

answers: The wicked will lose power while the righteous will be exalted
Both groups will keep equal power
The righteous will lose power while the wicked rise
challenge.explanation: The final verse reverses their fortunes: the wicked are cut off and the righteous are lifted up.
challenge.q: What does the change from the wicked’s horns to the righteous’ horns signify?

paragraphs.idea: The Lord’s cup contains mixed wine and represents judgment. The wicked drink its dregs, while the psalmist promises to declare God’s works and sing praises; the wicked’s horns will be cut off, but the righteous will be exalted.
